# Interesting Creative AI Projects Since March 2023

Here's a curated summary of some of the most notable and interesting creative projects made with AI:

---

## Film & Video

- **"Thank You for Not Answering" & early AI short films** – A wave of AI-generated short films emerged using tools like Runway Gen-2, Pika Labs, and later Sora (OpenAI). Filmmakers began blending AI-generated footage with traditional editing.
- **"The Frost" (2023)** – A short film by Waymark that was one of the early narrative films made largely with generative AI tools.
- **Sora demo films (2024)** – OpenAI's Sora text-to-video model produced stunning demo clips that went viral, sparking debate about the future of filmmaking.
- **"Air Head" by Shy Kids** – An acclaimed AI-generated short film using Sora, featuring a man with a balloon for a head. Premiered at SXSW 2024.
- **Coca-Cola's AI holiday ad (2023)** – A controversial recreation of their classic "Holidays Are Coming" ad using generative AI.

## Music

- **"Heart on My Sleeve" (2023)** – A viral AI-generated song mimicking Drake and The Weeknd by creator Ghostwriter, which ignited massive debate about AI in music and copyright.
- **Grimes' open AI voice policy** – Grimes invited anyone to use her AI-cloned voice and split royalties 50/50, pioneering a new model for artist-AI collaboration.
- **Google DeepMind's Lyria & "Dream Track"** – YouTube's experiment letting creators generate short music clips in the style of consenting artists.
- **Udio & Suno** – AI music generation platforms that emerged in late 2023/2024, capable of producing remarkably convincing full songs across genres with just text prompts.
- **"BBL Drizzy" (2024)** – A comedic AI-generated diss track that went viral during the Drake/Kendrick Lamar feud, made with AI tools.

## Visual Art & Design

- **Refik Anadol's "Unsupervised" at MoMA** – A large-scale AI artwork installed at the Museum of Modern Art, using machine learning trained on MoMA's collection to create living, evolving digital sculptures.
- **AI Fashion Week (2023)** – The world's first AI fashion week where designers submitted AI-generated clothing collections (via Midjourney, DALL·E, etc.), with winning designs actually manufactured.
- **Midjourney V5/V6 & DALL·E 3 photorealism wave** – Artists pushed these tools to create hyperrealistic and surreal imagery, blurring lines between photography and generation.
- **"Théâtre D'opéra Spatial" aftermath** – Jason Allen's AI-generated art (which won a state fair competition in 2022) continued to fuel debate; his copyright claim was denied by the US Copyright Office, becoming a landmark case.
- **Boris Eldagsen's photography protest (2023)** – Won the Sony World Photography Award with an AI-generated image, then refused the prize to spark a conversation about AI in art.

## Writing & Literature

- **"Death of an Author" by Stephen Marche (2023)** – Billed as the first novel written with AI assistance, exploring the creative process with LLMs.
- **Numerous AI-assisted poetry and fiction projects** – Writers like Sheila Heti, Robin Sloan, and others have publicly experimented with using LLMs as creative collaborators.
- **NaNoWriMo controversy (2024)** – The National Novel Writing Month organization controversially declined to take a hard stance against AI-written entries.

## Interactive & Experimental

- **AI Dungeon & narrative AI games** – Continued evolution of open-ended AI storytelling games.
- **"1000 Bots" project** – Various artists created armies of AI personas/chatbots as art installations and social experiments.
- **Worldbuilding with AI** – Creators began using tools like ChatGPT + Midjourney + Suno together to build entire fictional universes with lore, visuals, music, and interactive elements.
- **AI-generated podcasts (Google NotebookLM)** – In late 2024, Google's NotebookLM feature to auto-generate realistic podcast-style discussions from documents went viral, with people creating oddly compelling "podcasts" about everything from their resumes to academic papers.

## Architecture & 3D

- **AI-assisted architecture** – Firms like Zaha Hadid Architects began integrating AI tools into design workflows, and solo creators used AI to generate stunning speculative architecture.
- **3D generation tools (Meshy, Tripo, etc.)** – Text/image-to-3D tools matured significantly, enabling creators to generate usable 3D models from prompts.

## Performance & Theater

- **"AI: When a Robot Writes a Play" and similar stage works** – Experimental theater productions featuring scripts partially or wholly generated by AI, exploring themes of authorship and creativity.

## Games

- **AI-assisted indie game development** – Solo developers and small teams used AI for concept art, dialogue, music, and even code to produce games that would have previously required much larger teams.
- **Minecraft & AI world generation** – Projects like Google DeepMind's GENIE and others explored AI-generated playable game worlds.

---

## Key Themes

- **Democratization** – People with no formal training in art, music, or film began producing polished creative work.
- **Copyright battles** – Nearly every domain saw heated legal and ethical debates (the NYT lawsuit, visual artists' class actions, music licensing fights).
- **"Full-stack" creators** – A new archetype emerged: individuals using multiple AI tools together to create entire multimedia projects solo.
- **Backlash & resistance** – Many creative communities pushed back hard, with platforms banning AI work and organizations taking stances against it.
- **Human-AI collaboration** – The most critically praised projects tended to be those where AI was a tool in a clearly human-directed creative vision, rather than pure generation.

---

Would you like me to dive deeper into any particular category?
